Title: Cast to index signature (question)
Description: Each ES object is a dictionary of string keys.
Therefore it is allowed to write either a.b or a["b"] in ES.

TS doesn't allow this unless you specify index signature.
Also you cannot cast to this type without casting to 'any' .

``` typescript
var q: { a: number; } = { a: 1 };

// This is not allowed since 'q' type is not assignable to this type.
(<{[x:string]:any}>q)["a"] = 2;

// This is allowed since any can be casted to anything.
(<{[x:string]:any}><any>q)["a"] = 2;
```

'Object' type from lib.d.ts doesn't have index signature either, so you cannot use it as well.
Is there anything better than casting to 'any' ?
